bites.title: Conditionals
bites.body: if, elif, and else choose a path. Python uses indentation, not braces, to show which lines belong to a branch. The first true condition runs, and the rest are skipped. A missing indent is a syntax error. When you read generated code, check that each branch is indented under the right condition and that a later elif is not impossible.
bites.sourceNote: Python tutorial, if statements · confidence: high
bites.diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Look at the condition"] --> B{"Is it true?"}
  B -->|Yes| C["Run the if branch"]
  B -->|No| D["Run the else branch"]
  C --> E["Continue"]
  D --> E

questions.prompt: score is 80. The code checks if score > 90, then elif score > 70. Which branch runs?
questions.explanation: 80 is not greater than 90, so the if is skipped. 80 is greater than 70, so the elif runs.

questions.prompt: How does Python know which lines belong to an if branch?

choices.text: By a semicolon at the end

questions.explanation: A consistent indent marks the block. The next line that is outdented is outside the branch.

bites.title: Loops and iteration
bites.body: A for loop walks a collection one item at a time: for name in names. range(3) yields 0, then 1, then 2 — it stops before 3. A while loop repeats as long as its condition stays true. If that condition never becomes false, the loop never ends. Generated loops are worth tracing with a tiny collection before you trust them.
bites.sourceNote: Python tutorial, for and while · confidence: high

questions.prompt: How many times does for n in range(3) run the body?
questions.explanation: range(3) produces 0, 1, and 2. That is three passes, and 3 itself is not included.

questions.prompt: When does a while loop stop?

choices.text: Only if you use for instead

questions.explanation: Before each pass, Python checks the condition. A false condition ends the loop.
